slides.title:
At 14, he *delivered*
shirts. Then he
built Zara.
slides.sub:
Today: €39.9 billion in sales a year.
How Amancio Ortega did it 👇

slides.title:
He leaves school to
work as a *delivery boy*
for a shirt shop.
slides.sub:
In A Coruña, Spain. The shop was
200 metres from where the first
Zara would open (Ara).

slides.title:
With his family, he
starts making clothes.
First hit: *bathrobes*.
slides.sub:
The company: Confecciones Goa.
He's 27 (Britannica, Ara,
Encyclopedia.com).

slides.title:
May 1975: first store.
The name he wanted
was *already taken*.
slides.sub:
So he went with Zara. Juan Flórez
Street, A Coruña (Ara).

slides.title:
From runway to store
in *a few weeks*. New
styles arrive every week.
slides.sub:
Fewer pieces, more variety, more often.
And very little advertising
(Britannica, Encyclopedia.com).

slides.title:
Ortega *called his store
managers* every week
and asked what they needed.
slides.sub:
And he went to the warehouse himself
(Pau Almar, quoted by Ara).

slides.title: Zara has proven that *speed and flexibility* matter more than pure price.
slides.author:
John Thorbeck, supply-chain
consultant (Newsweek, 2001)

slides.title:
Inditex 2025 sales.
*€6.2B* net profit.
5,460 stores, 214 markets.
slides.sub:
Online alone: €10.7B (Inditex FY2025,
via FashionUnited, Inside Retail).

slides.title:
Sell what your
customers *ask for*.
slides.sub:
Zara didn't guess. It asked every week,
then moved fast.
